WBTVBQ.position: You bought this building in 2013, near the bottom of the cycle, at a basis of ±$37 per square foot — and the market has spent thirteen years proving you right. Today the same square footage trades at five times that number, and your building carries an advantage most of the competition can't match: it sits at the I-215/Mill St interchange, with tens of thousands of cars a day passing a building that never has to advertise its location. Sub-35,000 SF freeway-adjacent warehouses almost never come to market in central San Bernardino, and the owner-users and investors who need one have nowhere else to look. That scarcity is your leverage, and you hold every option an investor wants: sell into that demand at the top of the range, exchange into a larger or more passive asset through a 1031, or simply hold and mark the rent to today's market. Whichever direction you choose, the equity is already there — the only question is when and how you capture it.
WBTVBQ.comps_source: C&W / CoStar verified sales, Inland Empire 10k–100k SF, trailing 18 months (July 2026 set)
